references.text: Describes the anointing of the altar of burnt offering and its consecration, where the altar becomes most holy and everything that touches it becomes holy.
Instructions to anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils to consecrate them, so that they become most holy.
The description of how the altar of burnt offering was to be built, with all its utensils and equipment.
The actual construction of the altar of burnt offering and its utensils, which were now to be anointed and consecrated.
Moses anoints the tabernacle and the altar with anointing oil and sprinkles oil on the altar seven times to consecrate it.
Refers to the day when Moses completed setting up the tabernacle and anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils.
The dedication offerings for the altar after it had been anointed confirm the altar's holy status.
Ezekiel's vision of the future altar that is to be cleansed and dedicated over seven days to become most holy.
Jesus teaches about the holiness of the altar and how the altar sanctifies the gift placed on it.
The book of Hebrews mentions that Moses sprinkled blood on the tabernacle and all the utensils used in worship.
Complementary descriptions of the dedication of the altar and the consequence of its becoming most holy.
Extends the principle of consecration from the altar to the priests by using identical language regarding the consequence.
Links atonement and anointing as necessary actions for the consecration of the altar.
